title: Make the project's CI check pass (lint + a failing test), commit

turns.prompt: {D}/tally is a small Python package with a CI check script, `./check.sh`, that currently fails. Run it, fix everything it complains about in the package code (do not edit check.sh or the tests), run it again until it passes, and commit with a message starting `fix:`. Tell me what was wrong.
turns.verify: cd {D}/tally && out=$(./check.sh 2>&1); rc=$?; locked=$(sha256sum tests/test_tally.py check.sh | cut -d' ' -f1 | tr '\n' ' '); n=$(git log --oneline | wc -l); msg=$(git log -1 --pretty=%s); echo "SHOW rc=$rc commits=$n last='$msg' locked_unchanged=$([ "$locked" = "$(cat ../.locked_sha)" ] && echo yes || echo no)"; echo "SHOW $out" | tail -3; if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ "$locked" = "$(cat ../.locked_sha)" ] && [ $n -ge 2 ] && echo "$msg" | grep -qi '^fix'; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL: rc=$rc commits=$n; fi
